name: Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis Type 1 (CLN1 Disease)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis Type 1

criteria.description: Progressive psychomotor regression with onset in infancy
Deficiency of palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1 (PPT1) enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in the PPT1 gene
Detection of characteristic granular osmiophilic deposits in lymphocytes or skin biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive psychomotor regression plus either enzyme deficiency or pathogenic PPT1 gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical for genetic counseling and potential future therapies.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically begins between 6 and 24 months of age

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visual loss due to retinal degeneration
pathognomonic.notes: Rapidly progressive vision impairment leading to blindness
searchTerms: loss of sight due to retina problems

common.symptomName: Ataxia and loss of motor coordination

common.notes: Loss of previously acquired language skills

occasional.notes: May precede or accompany neurological decline
Including insomnia and altered sleep-wake cycles

rare.notes: Mild enlargement of liver and spleen

laboratory: Reduced palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1 (PPT1) enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Elevated levels of lipofuscin-like autofluorescent storage material in peripheral blood lymphocytes
imaging: Brain MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating retinal thinning
genetic: Pathogenic variants in the PPT1 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Electron microscopy revealing granular osmiophilic deposits in skin or conjunctival biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Later onset (2-4 years) compared to CLN1
Different genetic mutations in TPP1 gene
Slower progression and different clinical features

redFlags: Rapidly progressive psychomotor regression in infancy
Early onset visual loss with retinal degeneration
Refractory myoclonic seizures in a young child
references: Mole SE, Williams RE. Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinoses. GeneReviews. 2020.
